title: Dizzy Gillespie as a person; looking at him in Europe
summary: Dizzy stayed healthy and sweet; he sensed Mingus's love from across a room.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah. You were talking about Bud and Bird before. And I was thinking the other day, here's Dizzy, 60 years old, he's done better than survive, I mean, he's --
And he's still healthy, too.
Yeah, and he's -- his temperament is good. Why did he -- was he able to stay intact and the others weren't, do you think?
Well, he (unintelligible) everybody
else does. Dizzy is a sweet guy, I was told.
Yeah.
All the guys loved him in the big bands.
Have you had much conversation with him?

We've talked, very little. But I remember, in Europe, I was just sitting, looking at him, one time, from a distance. And he turned around and said, man, I'm feeling all this love come in. Says, you really love me, don't you? I feel like I was in heaven, and saw you staring at me. And I was. I was thinking about, I hope he lived forever, and how important he was.
Gee, that's interesting that that kind of emotion can be transmitted that way. Because you weren't saying anything.
Nothing.
And his back was towards you.
I was thinking all these things.
Yeah.
His back was turned.
Yeah.
Ask him about it sometime.
I will, yeah. I know you played with him in a concert at Massey Hall. Any other times?
Only -- no, that's about it. He came
and sat in at the -- Mingus' Friends in Concert.
Oh, yeah.
He came and sat in.
